reasons: The resource section requests 28 tasks with 1 core each (`#flux: -n 28`, `#flux: -c 1`), but the intended workload is a single NAMD process using 28 threads (`namd2 +p28`). This should be represented as 1 task with 28 cores to avoid misallocation.

The original Slurm job required 2 K80 GPUs (`--gres=gpu:k80:2`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.
The original Slurm job requested exclusive node access (`--exclusive`) but the Flux resource section has no exclusivity request; node sharing may introduce contention and performance variability.
issues: The launch command `flux run -n 1 -c 28 ...` conflicts with the batch allocation (`#flux: -n 28 -c 1`), which can lead to oversubscription or launch failure depending on Flux configuration.
